method: Three strand sets share exactly the same x/y centerlines, hence the same orthographic front projection. Only the z coordinates of the marked OCCLUDED tail differ. A side projection exposes the ambiguity.

checks.name: front projection is identical for reference and prior A
front projection is identical for reference and prior B
side projection exposes prior A difference
side projection exposes prior B difference
occluded prior A is materially different
occluded prior B is materially different
front-only disclosed prior is held, not promoted
withheld side mismatch rejects the candidate

boundary: Synthetic observability counterexample only; it is not a DiffLocks quality measurement.
It proves non-identifiability under a front projection, not that every generated backside is wrong.
A plausible learned prior may be useful as an explicitly labeled candidate, but cannot be promoted as reference truth without additional evidence or user authorization.
